### Accordion align

In rare cases, you may need to specify the alignment of the icon in the
accordion. You can use the `align` prop to specify the side where the icon
should be placed.

_Note: This prop must not be used to create a tree view or set of nested
accordions._

```jsx
<Accordion align="start">
  <AccordionItem title="Panel A">Panel A</AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem title="Panel B">Panel B</AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem title="Panel C">Panel C</AccordionItem>
</Accordion>

## References

### Why is interactive content in a heading considered an accessibility violation?

When using the `title` prop from `Accordion`, it is possible to render arbitrary
markup within the accordion header. The accordion header itself is rendered as a
`<button>` and is considered an interactive element.

If you render an interactive element inside this header, then it becomes nested
inside the `<button>`. Common examples of this are buttons or links. Rendering
interactive content inside the accordion heading is not reachable via a keyboard
or screen reader.

synthesis.guidance: Use accordions for independently expandable sections in dense product screens, not hierarchical navigation that requires a real tree pattern. The inspected docs allow changing disclosure-icon side with align but explicitly reject using it to fake a tree view. Treat the title as one interactive button's label: place edit, help, download or overflow actions outside that heading. Separate those actions spatially on the same baseline with restrained dividers, so a functional row does not become a decorative card. Give the body a readable line length and preserve keyboard focus visibility. The second excerpt is an actionable accessibility constraint, not source to render. Full Apache license is retained; no IBM fonts, pictograms, icons or Sass bundle were copied.

synthesis.summary: Carbon warns that accordion headings are buttons: nested links or buttons are unreachable for keyboard or screen-reader users. Icon alignment must not be used to simulate a tree view.
